## Requirements: Xterm Engine architecture and Terminal component boundaries

### Background / owner decision (2026-10-29)

Following a source-level review of Nession's Web/App terminal implementation and comparison with VS Code's xterm integration, **keep the current terminal line-height and visual spacing unchanged**. This is an internal architecture / dependency ownership requirement, not a visual retuning or a replacement of the established terminal correctness model.

Current baseline on `main`:
- `web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/controller/TerminalController.ts` (~1,293 lines) coordinates xterm mounting, transport rewiring, ordered writer/bootstrap, repair, sizing, input, IME, and viewport behavior. It is becoming the integration point for unrelated concrete implementations.
- `instance/TerminalInstance.ts` constructs xterm and configures renderer/theme/font; `Renderer.ts` manages WebGL/Canvas lifecycle; `grid.ts` reaches into `_core._renderService` for cell metrics.
- `product/terminal/components/TerminalViewport.tsx` accesses `controller.terminal` and registers an xterm link provider directly, crossing the product/engine abstraction.
- `product/terminal/workspaceFileLinks.ts` maps JS string offsets to terminal cell positions; wide Unicode, combining cells and wrapped lines require explicit correctness coverage.
- `controller/TerminalController.ts` contains `ResizeController`; geometry calculation can repeat font measurement on height-only changes.
- `input/MobileImeInput.ts` and interaction/scroll helpers still need their xterm access inventoried and mediated by the engine contract where practical.
- Existing `SessionRuntime` is already the single transport/attach lifecycle authority per #1309. `SerializedTerminalWriter`, `AppliedTerminalCursor`, replay/bootstrap and multi-client ControlLease behavior already have their own owners. **Do not reimplement or fork any of them.**

Related completed requirements: #649 (Web layering), #256 (PC/mobile shared terminal), #1096 (PTY-faithful interaction), #1309 (runtime authority), #1645 / #1927 (stream correctness), #2286 / #2487 / #2557 (active-controller/fixed-column sizing). This is a **new internal emulator-adapter/component-boundary decision**, not a reopening of those completed invariants.

### Goals and architectural contract

Establish one **business-neutral Xterm Engine**, initially **internal to** `platform/terminal-runtime/xterm/`, providing a narrow emulator/renderer/metrics/extension API. No npm package extraction in this requirement. The public concept should be named by responsibility (e.g. `TerminalEmulator` port + `XtermEmulator` adapter), not by a second Session or transport runtime.

Proposed ownership:

```text
app / product/terminal (TerminalViewport, Capsule, Workspace links)
  |  presentation + feature intentions, no raw xterm or transport decisions
  v
platform/terminal-runtime/view (thin terminal view composition)
  +-- TerminalGeometry: fixed cols, measured-cell font fit, rows; product inset is a supplied measurement
  +-- TerminalInteraction: PTY-semantic key/text/paste/mouse/IME intents
  +-- TerminalStreamAdapter: applies already-ordered stream/bootstrap to emulator
  +-- SerializedTerminalWriter: sole FIFO of buffer/grid mutations and parser completion
  |
  v
platform/terminal-runtime/xterm
  +-- XtermEmulator: xterm instance, mount/reparent/unmount/dispose, buffer and parser adapter
  +-- XtermMetrics: measured cell/grid/cursor read model; isolate private API fallback
  +-- XtermRenderer / XtermAddonHost: WebGL/Canvas/addon installation and teardown
  |
  ^ immutable runtime facts / typed events / transport binding
  |
platform/session-runtime/SessionRuntime (SOLE session/route/attach/lease authority)
  +-- existing ConnectionManager / TerminalTransport / StreamReconciler
  +-- existing AppliedTerminalCursor, replay and ACK policy
```

This diagram describes responsibilities, **not mandatory file creation**. Keep existing small cohesive modules where suitable; avoid extra trivial façade classes. Follow `docs/architecture/web.md` (app → product → platform → shared), the no-reverse-imports gate, and React-free `platform/terminal-runtime`.

#### 1. Xterm Engine contract

The adapter is the sole production owner of the raw `@xterm/xterm` `Terminal` instance and renderer-specific APIs. Define minimal ports for:
- `mount / unmount / dispose` and host reparenting without destroying the terminal buffer;
- ordered `write/resize/clear/bootstrap` application **only through the existing serialized writer path**, with parser-completed notifications;
- measured cell/grid/cursor information and bounded font/theme configuration;
- disposable `onData/onBinary` (or an equivalent correctly typed byte-safe interface), mode/read-only snapshot, and link/addon registration.

Do **not** allow a broad `getRawTerminal()` escape hatch in Product/UI. If raw xterm is genuinely required by a specialized adapter, keep access confined to `xterm/` with an explicit ownership reason.

Audit `grid.ts` private access. Prefer xterm public APIs verified against the actual pinned version; isolate necessary proposed/private APIs in one compatibility adapter, with version-pinned negative/regression tests. Do not assume a newer xterm API is present in the installed version.

#### 2. View Controller / Geometry boundary

Reduce `TerminalController` to view-scoped composition: attach/detach, coordinate collaborators, expose typed Product ports, and report viewport facts upward. It must not own route/retry/recovery decisions.

`TerminalGeometry` owns the **already-approved** fixed-column font fit, measured cell width, usable height/rows and resize requests. The Product layer supplies available box measurements/capsule occlusion; platform must not reinterpret Product CSS policy. A height-only change must not repeatedly refit font width. Deduplicate no-op grid writes without violating ordering, xterm state, or agent-authoritative resize facts.

Keep columns as the **live Session/Agent-authored** value, regardless of build defaults. Do not change 96-column release policy, font sizes, line height, or visual tokens in this refactor.

#### 3. Input and extension boundaries

Retain #1096's single PTY semantic authority: physical keyboard, mobile IME, capsule/accessory keys, paste and pointer events use one interaction path. The UI acquires intent; the terminal state determines VT bytes. Preserve bracketed paste, application cursor modes, TUI mouse, Ctrl+D as data, and composed text; do not write application-specific escape tables. If supporting `onBinary`, preserve byte identity end-to-end rather than coercing arbitrary bytes through UTF-8 strings.

Move xterm addon/link registration behind a scoped disposable interface. Product owns Workspace file-link recognition and navigation action; xterm adapter owns `registerLinkProvider` and cell mapping. Establish correct link positions for Unicode width, combining characters, and wrap, or explicitly constrain unsupported matching with deterministic tests. All subscriptions and Addons are disposed exactly once under StrictMode/reparent/renderer recovery.

#### 4. Stream correctness is preserved, not relocated

Preserve `SerializedTerminalWriter`'s FIFO and bounds, valid bootstrap fidelity/cut semantics, parser-completed callback identity, old-generation rejection, stream cursor / ACK authorization, overflow repair, and reparent scrollback. The Engine reports **parse/apply facts only**; SessionRuntime retains authoritative stream synchronization/recovery/ACK decisions. No new React/Jotai writable copy of lifecycle state, no direct `terminal.write` or `terminal.resize` bypass around writer ordering, and no direct transport sends from Product components.

### Migration plan (incremental, independently reviewable)

1. **Boundary inventory / RFC:** document every raw xterm import, write/resize site, addon and disposable, state owner, dependency edge and target port; distinguish verified defects from unproven risks. Record canonical ownership and public API under `docs/design/terminal/` / `docs/architecture/`.
2. **Emulator adapter:** introduce the narrow internal port and xterm-specific implementation, migrate `TerminalInstance` / Renderer / metrics / add-on lifecycle without changing visible behavior; add lint/architectural negative fixtures for forbidden imports/private access.
3. **Product/interaction adapters:** migrate `TerminalViewport`, Workspace Links, IME and optional addons to typed disposable ports; prohibit UI imports of raw xterm.
4. **Controller convergence:** split Geometry / Stream Apply / Interaction responsibilities only after they have tests; reduce Controller to composition while retaining exact SessionRuntime identity/binding and writer order.
5. **Behavioral regression / docs:** source-aligned unit/integration + selected browser E2E on exact PR head; document final dependency graph. Split separately reviewable PRs/child Issues as needed; **do not** switch correctness ownership during an incremental migration.

### Constraints / non-goals

- No new Terminal product UI or navigation pattern; no line-height adjustment. Do not alter fixed-column behavior, Web/App layout, existing terminal mode semantics or release configuration.
- No reimplementation of SessionRuntime, ConnectionManager, StreamReconciler, ControlLease, tmux/Agent protocol, output ACK, or writer recovery logic.
- No speculative generic plugin framework, broad type-casts, public raw-terminal escape hatch, or mandatory new npm package.
- No large-bang rewrite, no double state authority, no xterm event subscription leaks, no weakened existing E2E/Acceptance checks.
- This requirement concerns **frontend xterm/component structure** only; backend tmux SDK work remains owned by #2469.

### Prototype
- **Decision:** Not needed
- **Reason / interaction uncertainty:** Internal architecture/refactor; no new user-facing interaction or desktop/mobile UX choice.
- **Scenario to validate:** Existing Session → desktop attach → TUI/IME/paste → mobile takeover → reconnect/route swap → same working terminal semantics/history.
- **Status:** Not needed
- **Artifact:** None; existing #2487 sizing simulator is reference only, not acceptance evidence.

### Verification scope
- **Proposed tier:** `verification:integration` (L2): lifecycle, renderer and stream/geometry/interaction ports cross browser and session boundaries. Use selected browser tests; **no blanket full E2E or main-only gate**. Smaller child PRs may use narrower L1 evidence when isolated.
- **Earliest evidence:** PR-head source checks/unit cases for boundary and adapter behavior; PR-head full-stack browser Cases for attach, input, recovery, and route transitions. Do not require production credentials or substitute an unexecuted Agent verdict for a Case.

### Knowledge Impact
- **Decision:** Create (unless query of the live knowledge index discovers an existing article owning the same concept).
- **Related knowledge:** Current knowledge index on the independent `knowledge` branch (searched `terminal` / `architecture`; no current terminal-topic article observed); canonical `docs/design/terminal/session-runtime-ownership.md`, `interaction-semantics.md`, `terminal-sizing.md`, `docs/architecture/web.md`.
- **Reason:** The isolated emulator adapter / view ownership / addon-lifecycle rules are a durable internal architecture decision distinct from prior session transport and terminal semantics docs.
- **Owner and timing:** Web Terminal implementation owner + reviewer, publish/reconcile a single sourced terminal architecture article on the governed `knowledge` branch after implementation decision and before final acceptance; add article/index/global changelog atomically, with exact commit source and validation.
- **Evidence:** This Requirement; implementation PR #2583; the architecture doc and source-aligned runtime test receipts; knowledge article published at https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/commit/a8ad3c70cdd303d70aeaff5554a0d05e0b5285af (topic `terminal`, created from the exact implementation commit and validated by `knowledge-ledger-contract`).

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 Canonical design doc identifies exactly one writable owner for session lifecycle, xterm instance, ordered buffer/grid mutation, geometry policy, input semantics, addon disposal and Product link parsing; the final dependency graph matches the implemented imports.
- [ ] SC-02 A machine-checked architectural rule rejects production Product/UI direct `@xterm/xterm` imports, xterm `_core` access outside the single compatibility adapter, and direct bypass of the ordered writer; negative fixture proves each rejected case while legitimate adapter access is allowed.
- [ ] SC-03 One emulator instance survives viewport detach/reparent/reattach and React StrictMode replay without duplicate input/listener/addon subscriptions or lost scrollback; disposal releases all owned resources exactly once.
- [ ] SC-04 WebGL/Canvas initialization, renderer failure fallback and addon install/dispose preserve a usable terminal with no stale callbacks; deterministic failure-injection checks exercise the fallback and reinstallation path.
- [ ] SC-05 Product Workspace Links are installed through an emulator port (not `controller.terminal`); link activation and cell coordinates are correct for supported ASCII, wide-character/combining text and wrapped-line cases, with explicit safe behavior for unsupported matches.
- [ ] SC-06 Fixed Session columns remain unchanged across viewport width/height, capsule occlusion, font fit, and active-device transitions; height-only events do not re-run width-fit and unchanged geometry generates no redundant local mutation or remote resize.
- [ ] SC-07 Desktop keyboard, Mobile IME, semantic keys, paste, mouse and applicable binary input produce exactly one ordered PTY-bound input with correct VT mode semantics through attach, detach and transport rewire; no byte corruption.
- [ ] SC-08 Output/bootstrap/resize still use the existing bounded FIFO; callbacks are parser-completed before applied-cursor ACK eligibility, and stale transport/renderer callbacks cannot mark the new generation synchronized. Overflow/repair and incomplete bootstrap retain fail-closed behavior.
- [ ] SC-09 The same visible terminal state/history and correct Controller/Observer ownership survive desktop↔mobile takeover, P2P↔Relay swap and reconnect, without duplicate or missing output under source-aligned fault/route fixtures.
- [ ] SC-10 Fixture and production terminal construction consume the same emulator/renderer/metrics rules where behavior overlaps; lint, unit, integration and scoped browser regressions are source-aligned and run on the exact PR revision; final architecture docs and knowledge-impact decision are updated with verifiable evidence.
